analysis:
The two supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 218-770), which describe prior releases (v0.10.0 to v0.10.1 and the tail of the previous v0.10.x section). The PR's actual change is documentation only: it replaces the v0.10.4 candidate header with a v0.10.5 candidate section at head lines 11-176. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the head text was not supplied. I therefore could not examine most of the new v0.10.5 content. It mentions MLX pin bumps, a metallib hash change, per-build complete SSD checkpoint namespaces, and the `darkbloom sandbox` installer and add-on flow.

The base text I examined is historical release-note prose. It touches several areas relevant to the threat model: SSD prefix cache (T-041), Autopilot downloads and holds, and the desktop control API. Changelog text is not executable and does not change controls. Nothing in the base excerpt shows a security regression. The base lines also cannot support a claim about the head's behavior.

The visible patch lines about the sandbox add-on installer (`api-sandbox.darkbloom.dev/install.sh` run as the owner) are relevant to TB-013, A-019 and T-061, but the excerpt only describes existing documented behavior. It is not a code change. Remaining integration questions: whether the actual code changes in this PR (the MLX pins, the sandbox CLI, the checkpoint namespace binding) are in other batches and whether they keep the T-041 posture of HMAC-keyed names, a 30-minute TTL and KEK scoping. Per-build checkpoint namespaces binding the binary and metallib hashes do not appear to loosen the at-rest posture. Because the head text is not visible and the patch is truncated, I set needs_deeper_review to true as a coverage limit, not as evidence of a problem.
